diseases.sectionSubtitle: Learn about diagnoses, symptoms, and solutions

items.name: Tinnitus
items.description: The perception of ringing, buzzing, or noise in the ears without an external sound source.

items.name: Age-Related Hearing Loss
items.description: The natural decline in hearing ability with age. It is one of the most common hearing problems.

items.name: Noise-Induced Hearing Loss
items.description: Permanent hearing loss caused by prolonged exposure to high levels of noise.

items.name: Ménière's Disease
items.description: An inner-ear fluid imbalance that can cause vertigo, tinnitus, and fluctuating hearing loss.
symptoms: A feeling of fullness in the ear

items.name: Otosclerosis
items.description: Abnormal bone hardening in the middle ear that restricts the movement of the small bones and can lead to progressive hearing loss.
symptoms: Hearing one's own voice unusually loudly

items.name: Congenital Hearing Loss
items.description: Hearing loss that may occur in infants and children. Early intervention with hearing aids is essential for hearing and speech development.
symptoms: No response to loud sounds between 0 and 3 months of age
No response when their name is called between 6 and 12 months of age
Delayed speech development after 1 year of age

hearingDevices.title: The Importance of Choosing and Using a Hearing Aid in Sarıyer
hearingDevices.description: Hearing loss is about more than simply being unable to hear sounds. It can have a profound impact on social life, mental health, and overall quality of life. Hearing aids help the brain process sounds again and can restore communication, confidence, and independence. Where you choose to obtain your hearing aid is more important than the brand or model, because your hearing care professional will support your rehabilitation over the years.

benefits.title: Brain Health
benefits.description: When hearing loss goes untreated, the brain may gradually lose its ability to recognize sounds. Over time, this can increase the risk of cognitive decline and memory problems.

benefits.title: Social Life
benefits.description: People who experience hearing difficulties often withdraw from social situations. Hearing aids make communication easier and may help reduce social isolation and the risk of depression.

benefits.title: Quality of Life
benefits.description: With hearing aids, you can reconnect with the people around you, improve your safety, and enjoy a more active and fulfilling daily life.

hearingDevices.closingTitle: Do not neglect your hearing loss.
hearingDevices.closingText: Early diagnosis and choosing the right hearing aid are among the most effective ways to protect your mental and emotional well-being.

hearingTest.title: Hearing Test and Assessment in Sarıyer
hearingTest.description: A hearing test is a basic assessment used to evaluate your current hearing levels and ear health. It identifies the frequencies and sound levels at which you may have difficulty hearing. Based on the results, our specialists provide an individualized assessment and, when necessary, recommend a suitable hearing aid or therapy plan. This helps clarify the type of hearing loss and determine the most effective course of action.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Everything you need to know about the use and care of hearing aids

items.question: What is the average lifespan of a hearing aid?
items.answer: With proper care and maintenance, hearing aids typically last 5 to 7 years. Factors such as moisture, dust, and earwax can affect device longevity.

items.question: Do hearing aids make your ears lazy?
items.answer: No. Hearing aids do not make your ears lazy; they help you hear sounds you have difficulty perceiving and assist your brain in adapting back to those sounds.

items.question: How should I clean and protect my hearing aid?
items.answer: Wipe your device daily with a soft, dry cloth. Keep it away from moisture and water, and follow your specialist's recommendations for cleaning and care.

items.question: Can I connect my hearing aid to my smartphone?
items.answer: Yes. Compatible hearing aids with Bluetooth can be wirelessly paired with your smartphone. Compatibility may vary depending on device model and phone.

items.question: Is it difficult to get used to hearing aids for the first time?
items.answer: Sounds may feel different in the beginning. The adjustment period varies from person to person; most users comfortably adapt within a few weeks.

sgkPage.stepsTitle: How do you get a hearing aid with SGK?

steps.title: Hospital examination and report
steps.text: An ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialist examines you and a hearing test is done. If you need a hearing aid, a medical report is issued.

steps.title: Coming to our centre
steps.text: You bring your report to our SGK-contracted centre. We assess your hearing again and decide together which type of hearing aid suits you.

steps.title: SGK procedures
steps.text: Our centre records your report in the SGK system and handles the approval; you do not need to go to SGK yourself.

steps.title: Ear mould and fitting
steps.text: We take an impression of your ear, have your custom mould made, and fit your hearing aid adjusted to your hearing.

steps.title: Adaptation and care
steps.text: We follow your adaptation and service your hearing aid at regular check-ups.

bring: The hearing aid report from the hospital
Your previous hearing aid and earlier test results, if you have them
notes: SGK pays the amount set according to your report. If the chosen hearing aid costs more, the patient pays the difference.
To receive SGK support for a new hearing aid, the period set by SGK must have passed since the previous one. Ask us for the current period and support amount.
A report is valid for a limited time, so we recommend coming to our centre soon after you receive it.

faq.q: Does SGK pay for the whole hearing aid?
faq.a: SGK pays the amount set according to your report. If the hearing aid you choose costs more, you pay the difference. We go through the options and prices with you at our centre.

faq.q: Where do I get the SGK report?
faq.a: An ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialist at a hospital issues the report after an examination and a hearing test. You can then come to our SGK-contracted centre with it.

faq.q: Do I need to go anywhere else for the SGK procedures?
faq.a: No. When you come to our centre with your report, we handle the procedures in the SGK system.

faq.q: How can I pay the amount SGK does not cover?
faq.a: You can pay the amount not covered by SGK by credit card. If your card limit is not enough, you can pay the rest in instalments in person at our centre. Call us for details.

therapyPage.title: Auditory Rehabilitation in Sarıyer
therapyPage.paragraph1: Addressing hearing difficulties involves more than simply fitting a hearing aid. Lasting success comes from supporting the process with appropriate rehabilitation methods. Hearing rehabilitation aims not only to improve hearing, but also to help individuals regain understanding and effective communication skills.
therapyPage.paragraph2: During auditory rehabilitation, the person experiencing hearing loss remains at the center of the process. Active patient participation is essential when setting goals and choosing the most suitable solutions. After the assessment, a personalized hearing loss management plan is created. This plan helps the patient take an active role in protecting and improving their hearing.
therapyPage.paragraph3: Rehabilitation does more than improve hearing; it can also support a person's quality of life. Regular device follow-ups, maintenance, and rehabilitation are carefully managed by the hearing center where the device was obtained.
therapyPage.paragraph4: If you experience any problems with your hearing aid, we strongly recommend contacting the center where you obtained it.

education.title: Let's Get to Know Hearing Aid Types
education.subtitle: Which device is right for you? Here is a simple guide:

ric.title: RIC - Receiver-in-Canal
ric.desc: Small and discreet. The speaker is in the ear canal, and the device is behind the ear. Provides natural sound quality. Ideal for mild to moderate hearing loss.

bte.title: BTE - Behind-The-Ear
bte.desc: The most powerful device type. Sits behind the ear and transmits sound into the ear via a tube. Suitable for all levels of hearing loss, from mild to profound. Easy to handle.

ite.title: ITE - In-The-Ear
ite.desc: Fills the outer part of the ear completely. Visible but easy to use. Suitable for mild-to-moderate and moderate-to-severe hearing loss. Changing batteries is easier.

itc.title: ITC - In-The-Canal
itc.desc: Sits partially in the ear canal. Smaller and less conspicuous than ITE. Suitable for mild to moderate hearing loss. Requires some dexterity.

cic.title: CIC - Completely-in-Canal
cic.desc: Almost invisible! Sits deep within the ear canal. For mild to moderate loss. Battery life is shorter due to its small size. Requires good manual dexterity.

openFit.title: Open-Fit
openFit.desc: Does not block the ear canal, allowing natural ventilation. Prevents your own voice from sounding muffled. Excellent for high-frequency hearing loss. Very comfortable.

cros.title: CROS/BiCROS
cros.desc: Specially designed for single-sided deafness. Transmits sound from the poorer ear to the better ear. BiCROS is used if there is hearing loss in both ears. Helps you hear your surroundings better.

channels.title: Number of Channels
channels.desc: Allows adjusting different frequencies of sound separately. More channels mean more precise tuning. 16+ channels are sufficient for most people.

programs.title: Number of Programs
programs.desc: Settings for different environments. Example: quiet room, noisy restaurant, listening to music. 4-6 programs are usually enough.

noiseReduction.title: Noise Reduction
noiseReduction.desc: Reduces background noise, making conversations easier to hear. Very important in crowded places.

directionalMic.title: Directional Microphone
directionalMic.desc: Focuses on sounds in front of you while reducing noise from behind. Highly beneficial during conversations.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.desc: Streams audio directly from your phone to your device. Used for calls, music, and video. Compatible with iPhone and Android.

tinnitus.title: Tinnitus Therapy
tinnitus.desc: Generates specific sounds for ringing in the ears. Helps mask tinnitus and provides relief.

ip68.title: IP68 Protection
ip68.desc: Water and dust resistant. Withstands sweat, rain, and moisture. Safe for daily use.

rechargeable.title: Rechargeable
rechargeable.desc: No need to change batteries. Charge at night, use all day. Ideal for those with reduced dexterity.

feedback.title: Feedback Cancellation
feedback.desc: Prevents the whistling sound made by the device. Important when talking on the phone or hugging someone.

binaural.title: Binaural (Two Ears)
binaural.desc: Your two devices connect and work in sync. Helps you better determine where a sound is coming from.

autoEnv.title: Automatic Environment Recognition
autoEnv.desc: The device detects your environment and changes settings automatically. No need to manually switch programs.

ai.title: AI-Powered
ai.desc: The device learns as you use it and adapts to your preferences. It gets a little better every day.

note.title: 💡 Important Note:
note.text: Technical specifications are important, but the most crucial aspect is finding the right device for you, programming it correctly, and ensuring you get maximum efficiency. Our expert team will recommend the most suitable device by considering your hearing condition, lifestyle, and budget. Book an appointment for a consultation!

earMouldPage.title: An Ear Mould Made for Your Ear
earMouldPage.intro: Many hearing aids are fitted with ready-made, numbered silicone domes: the closest of a few sizes is chosen. We take an impression of your ear instead and fit your hearing aid with a mould made only for the shape of your ear canal. After the purchase, we keep looking after your mould and hearing aid and follow your adaptation together with you.
earMouldPage.whatText: An ear mould is a small piece made to the shape of your ear canal and outer ear. It holds the part of the hearing aid that delivers sound into the ear. Because every ear is different, the mould is yours alone.
readyPoints: Chosen from a few standard sizes.
Can be fitted at once, without an impression.
Chosen by size, not by the shape of your ear canal.
customPoints: Made for you from an impression of your ear.
Aims to sit more securely in the ear, which can make all-day wear more comfortable.
Can help reduce the gaps that cause whistling (feedback).

steps.title: Hearing test and assessment
steps.text: We first test your hearing and decide together which type of hearing aid suits you.

steps.title: Taking an impression
steps.text: We place a soft impression material in your ear canal. It sets within a few minutes and is then removed.

steps.title: Making the mould
steps.text: Your mould is made to the impression taken.

steps.title: Fitting and adjustment
steps.text: The mould is attached to your hearing aid, we check how it sits in your ear, and the hearing aid is adjusted for you.

steps.title: Adaptation and care
steps.text: We follow your first weeks of getting used to it and service your mould and hearing aid at regular check-ups.

earMouldPage.devicesTitle: Which hearing aids use a mould?
earMouldPage.devicesText: Behind-the-ear (BTE) and receiver-in-canal (RIC) hearing aids can be used with a custom mould. In-the-canal (ITC, CIC) hearing aids are themselves made to an impression of your ear. We decide together which suits you after your hearing test.
carePoints: Wipe the mould every day with a dry, soft cloth.
If the sound opening gets blocked, do not try to clear it yourself; we will clean it at our centre.
The shape of the ear can change over time. If the mould feels loose or uncomfortable, come in for a check; we will make a new one if needed.

faq.q: What does taking an ear impression feel like?
faq.a: A soft material is placed in your ear canal and left for a few minutes. You may feel slight fullness in the ear; it takes only a short time.

faq.q: Why do you use a mould instead of a ready-made dome?
faq.a: Every ear canal is different. A mould made from an impression of your ear is prepared so that the hearing aid sits more securely and suits your ear.

faq.q: When should my mould be replaced?
faq.a: Come in for a check when the mould feels loose, becomes uncomfortable or whistling increases. We also check your mould at regular maintenance visits.

earMouldPage.ctaTitle: Let us find the right solution for your ear together
